footnotes: Columns denote number of activities stopped. Values are risk ratios (95% confidence intervals), except common-population risks, shown as percentages. ADL, activities of daily living.

Pooled intervals use safeguarded Hartung–Knapp uncertainty. Common-population risks share an attainable target population; category-specific risks use different eligible populations. Mexico had no comparable interval.
methods: Inclusion models predicted complete-case retention from age, sex, interview wave, initial engagement, activities stopped and started, prior self-rated health, functional limitations, depressive symptoms, multimorbidity, education, income, smoking, and availability of an earlier interview. Missing predictors entered with missing indicators. Stabilized weights used the marginal retention probability divided by the fitted inclusion probability. We truncated weights at the first and ninety-ninth percentiles and normalized them to mean one. Sensitivities used untruncated weights and a numerator specific to the number of activities stopped. Minimal-covariate models included optional covariates only when they were observed in at least ninety-five percent of outcome-observed eligible person-intervals.

Weighted standardized risks averaged fitted probabilities over participants initially engaged in at least two activities, giving an attainable common target for all three categories. Person-interval counts in these rows describe the target population. Category-specific standardization instead uses the population eligible for each category and is reported separately. Inclusion weighting addresses measured differences in retention and does not remove selection through survival to the second interview. New ADL limitation also requires survival and observed follow-up.

Death estimates were examined after omitting each contributing cohort. New ADL limitation had only three supporting cohorts, so each omission left fewer than three and did not support random-effects synthesis. England did not meet the required event support for the two-or-more category at the higher age thresholds. Smoking-omitted models included otherwise eligible participants, including the SHARE wave with structurally unavailable smoking data. Country structure and survey-weight analyses were confined to their supported cohorts. MHAS had no comparable interval and contributed only to wider-follow-up sensitivity analyses.

HRS, Health and Retirement Study; KLoSA, Korean Longitudinal Study of Aging; MHAS, Mexican Health and Aging Study; SHARE, Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe.

Exposure covers drinking or regular physical activity. Repeated assays compare stopping an activity with neither activity stopped, adjusting for the first assay. Glycated-hemoglobin samples differ by scale. The unrounded HDL upper confidence limit is below zero.
methods: The biomarker analysis assessed stopping drinking or regular physical activity. Immunometabolic burden combined standardized inflammatory, glycemic, and lipid measures from the first interview, with high-density lipoprotein oriented so that lower levels indicated greater burden. Antecedent-marker models related each measure to subsequently stopping an activity. Separate repeated-assay models compared follow-up measures by whether an activity stopped while adjusting for the first assay and available covariates. ELSA repeated assays spanned the first interview to the outcome visit, approximately four years. The glycated-hemoglobin analysis in native percentage-point units used a separate covariate-complete sample. These assay-specific populations and mixed findings do not establish a common biological mechanism for the three-activity measure.

title: Disease-specific outcomes
footnotes: CI, confidence interval. Each comparison is stopping any activity versus none stopped among participants free of the specified disease at the second interview and with observed follow-up.

All models use the matched disease-specific complete-case sample. Standard adjustment excludes current engagement indicators. The other model also holds current drinking, regular physical activity, and paid work status. Pooled intervals use safeguarded Hartung–Knapp uncertainty.
methods: Disease-specific analyses included participants without the specified diagnosis at the second interview and with known follow-up status for that diagnosis. Stopping any activity across drinking, regular physical activity, and paid work was compared with none stopped. Models used the standard covariates and then added current engagement indicators on the same disease-specific sample. Diagnoses were participant-reported and required survival and observed follow-up. Cohort support depended on adequate outcome events and non-events.
